sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and input folders
sections.what: Loads the tools and sets the input and output folders to defaults unless told otherwise.
sections.why: Lets the script run from a command line with set folders.
sections.watch_out: Default paths are relative, so running from the wrong folder means missing files.

sections.name: csv, ballCols, matchCols, balls
sections.title: CSV escaping and column lists
sections.what: Defines the helper that quotes commas, quotes and line breaks, and lists the ball and match columns.
sections.why: Keeps the column layout fixed so the fitting scripts read the same layout.
sections.watch_out: Column names and their order must match what the fitting scripts expect.

sections.name: matches
sections.title: Write match and ball rows
sections.what: Loops through every match file, writes one match row and one row per delivery, then writes the compressed files and reports the counts.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the file header.
sections.watch_out: The team names are taken from the first two participants, so a match with fewer than two will crash the run.

summary: Turns downloaded Indian Premier League match files into two small compressed tables, one of matches and one of deliveries.
purpose: Makes the match and ball data quick to load for fitting the models.
why: The file header says it uses the same adapter as ingest, so the rules match the app.
how: Reads each match file in order, parses it with the Cricsheet adapter, writes a row for the match and one per delivery, then compresses both tables into the output folder and prints the counts.
inputs: A raw data folder and an output folder.
outputs: ipl-balls.csv.gz and ipl-matches.csv.gz, plus a printed count.
risks: One bad match file stops the whole run. The tables depend on the adapter, so changing the adapter changes the output.
debug: Read the printed counts and the error, which names the failing file.
